elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 inserts an express right: "Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon written notice to TrueLink." This cures the ambiguity in Section 14, which previously only described wind-down timing following a Client "election to terminate".

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence imposes no minimum notice period at all ("at any time upon written notice"), which is within the 30-day ceiling. Note the retained Section 14 wind-down means services (and monthly fees in arrears) continue to the last day of the month following the notice month, so the effective date can fall 31-61 days out; the notice requirement itself, however, is nil.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 13, Section 14, nor the inserted sentence contains any refund obligation. To reach the preferred level the drafter would need operative words such as "TrueLink shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination"; the rationale's observation that fees are billed monthly in arrears is commercial context, not operative language.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: On the cited provisions, TrueLink's only no-cause exit is non-renewal at the end of a one-year term (Section 13); the automatic cut-off of Sections 2 and 3 is triggered only by Client breach/default, i.e. for cause. No mid-term convenience right for TrueLink appears in the rendered text.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 gives Client an express convenience right on written notice with no minimum period, i.e. below the 60-90 day fallback ceiling and therefore at least as favourable to us; the retained Section 14 mechanic (services continue to the last day of the month following the notice month) supplies the effective-date lag of roughly 31-61 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, penalty, or liquidated-damages charge appears in Sections 13 or 14 or in the inserted sentence, so there is nothing to cap. The Section 14 wind-down is continued service (at most about two months of monthly fees), not a termination charge, and in any event sits under the three-month ceiling.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 13 confines TrueLink's no-cause exit to delivering notice of intent not to renew prior to the end of the then-current one-year period; no mid-term convenience right for TrueLink is created or retained in the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Operation 2 renders: "unless Client delivers written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days, or TrueLink delivers such notice no later than ninety (90) days, prior to the end of said year" - i.e. TrueLink's notice must land at least 90 days before term end, curing the former mutual 30-day (walk-away) notice while preserving our shorter 30-day non-renewal notice.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: an express Client convenience right (operation 1), no early-termination fee anywhere to cap, TrueLink limited to end-of-term non-renewal, and TrueLink's notice extended to 90 days (operation 2).

Preferred level fails on one element only: there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Client's convenience termination. If the drafter wants the preferred position, add operative refund language; the arrears-billing argument in the rationale is not a substitute.

Minimality holds: two surgical edits - one inserted sentence stating the right that Section 14 only implied, and a split of the existing mutual non-renewal notice that preserves our favourable 30-day period. No survival tails, expense allocation, procedures, or unrelated additions were bolted on.

Intent is preserved: the term, auto-renewal cycle, breach-triggered cut-off of Sections 2 and 3, domain-ownership and migration timing all survive unchanged, and the Section 14 wind-down continues to govern the post-notice service period.

Drafting nit worth a second look (not an element failure): Section 13 retains "until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein," so a reader could argue termination rights are channelled exclusively through Section 12. Consider adding "or Section 14" to that cross-reference to remove any argument that the new convenience right is inoperative.

Optional improvement: the inserted sentence specifies no notice period while Section 14 fixes the effective date at the last day of the month following the notice month. That is favourable to us but leaves the interaction implicit; a short "; termination will take effect in accordance with this Section 14" would make the mechanic explicit without adding any new obligation.
